transcript:
Header: Recorded on 2025-12-18 15:00 PST | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (Zenith Head of Security), Tom Reynolds (IT Ops), Priya Desai (Compliance)
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan with Redwood - I'll hand over to Maya to go through the posture details...
[00:20] Maya Patel: Yeah thanks, Alicia, really appreciate your time. We'll start with the SOC 2 scope. Redwood's latest SOC 2 Type II covers our hosted API and control plane, plus Dedicated control plane when it's managed by Redwood. The report link is in the Trust Center, I can share after call.
[00:45] Alicia Gomez: Quick Q - does that SOC 2 cover private deployments where we self-manage the runtime in our VPC?
[01:02] Maya Patel: Good question. So ISO and SOC coverage is for our managed control plane / hosted offering; for private deployments we provide a controls mapping and you'll get the artifacts that apply - some controls shift to customer responsibility. We'll provide a shared mapping doc that shows which controls are Redwood-owned vs customer-managed.
[01:28] Tom Reynolds: When you say mapping, is that like a spreadsheet? 
[01:32] Maya Patel: Exactly, a spreadsheet with control IDs, description, and notes - we also annotate the evidence type (report, configuration, policy). We'll upload that to the Trust Center link.
[01:49] Alicia Gomez: Can you confirm retention for audit logs? We need 7 years for a subset of events per our policy.
[02:05] Jordan Lee: We support configurable retention. For hosted we have default 90 days for high-volume logs but we can extend retention for enterprise plans; for Dedicated and Private you can ship logs to your SIEM or configure log export to your account for long-term retention.
[02:28] Priya Desai: By ship to our SIEM, do you mean syslog or S3 export?
[02:33] Maya Patel: We support S3 exports, and pushing events via Kinesis or direct HTTP forwarders. We also offer an audit export API. There was a small note in the docs about event types - we'll include a full event schema in the mapping doc.
[02:53] Alicia Gomez: For encryption - KMS - we want customer-managed keys. Is that supported for both Hosted and Dedicated?
[03:05] Maya Patel: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported on Dedicated and Private; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default, and customer-managed KMS is available for enterprise contracts via bring-your-own-key (BYOK) integration + HSM options.
[03:26] Tom Reynolds: Do you do at-rest encryption for model artifacts and shard caches?
[03:30] Maya Patel: All persisted artifacts are encrypted at rest. Runtime KV cache is encrypted on disk in Dedicated/Private; in hosted the cache may be ephemeral in-memory and encrypted in transit.
[03:46] [loud background noise] Speaker 1: sorry was that my phone?
[03:53] Jordan Lee: No worries.
[04:05] Alicia Gomez: On SSO and provisioning - we use Okta, SAML + SCIM. How mature is your RBAC and SCIM support?
[04:18] Maya Patel: We have SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning for users and groups, and fine-grained RBAC for token scopes and route permissions. There have been a few naming differences in the API docs (SAMEL typo appears in older doc) - we'll make sure you get the updated endpoints.
[04:40] Priya Desai: Any limitations on service accounts for automated pipelines?
[04:45] Jordan Lee: Service accounts exist with machine tokens. You can scope them to models, environments, and have rotation policies via the console or API.
[04:58] Tom Reynolds: Talking about evidence - is there an audit log for all admin actions?
[05:05] Maya Patel: Yes all admin actions are logged: RBAC changes, key rotations, deployments, and routing policy changes. The UI surfaces change history and you can export the auditable events.
[05:20] Alicia Gomez: We also need to map controls to ISO27001 annex A, not just SOC 2. Do you provide that?
[05:29] Maya Patel: Yes, the controls mapping doc will contain SOC2 to ISO27001 crosswalk, with references to the evidence artifacts.
[05:40] [pause] Speaker 2: is the crosswalk automatic?
[05:43] Maya Patel: It's curated, not auto-mapped - security team reviewed it.
[06:00] Alicia Gomez: For data residency - we have EU patient data, must keep all PII in EU. Do you have EU regions?
[06:12] Jordan Lee: We do. Hosted offers EU regions with data residency controls, and Dedicated can be provisioned in your chosen region. For Private we can deploy on-prem or in your VPC within the EU. We'll note required regions in the controls doc.
[06:30] Priya Desai: Any third-party sub-processors we should be aware of?
[06:34] Maya Patel: We publish a sub-processor list in the Trust Center. Major providers include cloud infra vendors and observability vendors - we can provide the list and SOC2 evidence for them where applicable.
[06:50] Tom Reynolds: Regarding penetration testing and vulnerability management?
[06:55] Maya Patel: We conduct annual pentests and regular vulnerability scanning; reports are summarized in the Trust Center, with higher-level findings redacted for confidentiality.
[07:10] Jordan Lee: If you want raw reports we can do NDA workflow - common ask.
[07:16] Alicia Gomez: We'll probably need that if we run a pilot.
[07:20] [15:05] Maya Patel: switching gears - about Private deployment responsibilities: Some controls like physical security or customer network segmentation are by customer. We'll highlight each control.
[15:40] Tom Reynolds: Do you support dedicated hardware HSM for key storage?
[15:45] Maya Patel: Yes, HSM-backed KMS is an option for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we integrate with cloud KMS providers but we can discuss HSM for enterprise.
[16:01] Alicia Gomez: Can you show the Trust Center while we are on call?
[16:05] Jordan Lee: I shared the Trust Center link in chat - https://redwood-inference.com/trust-center - includes SOC2, ISO summary, sub-processor list, and mapping artifacts.
[16:22] Alicia Gomez: I saw the SOC2 2025 PDF - is that Type II?
[16:26] Maya Patel: Yes Type II for period Jan-June 2025, we rotate annually. We'll attach the Type II PDF to the follow-up email.
[16:39] Priya Desai: For rekeying - if we hold KMS keys, do you support key rotation without downtime?
[16:48] Maya Patel: Yes, we have rotation procedures that support seamless rotation using double-encryption steps and a staged roll-forward. We'll attach a short KB.
[17:00] Tom Reynolds: What about model weights - if we bring our own model to Private, is the inference runtime permitted to log any inputs?
[17:12] Maya Patel: For Private on-prem it's under your control - by default we don't log request payloads in detail; for hosted you can enable request logging but it's off by default, and you can configure tokenization redaction.
[17:28] Jordan Lee: Important point - we offer PII redaction hooks and pre-send filters as part of the ingestion pipeline.
[17:45] Alicia Gomez: SLA and liability - any limitations in your standard MSA?
[17:52] Jordan Lee: Standard MSA has uptime SLAs for Dedicated and Enterprise; we can discuss contractual addendums for data residency and specific liabilities with legal.
[18:05] Priya Desai: A question about control evidence - can we get screenshots or config dumps showing RBAC roles?
[18:14] Maya Patel: Yes we can provide sanitized config snapshots and RBAC role export for auditors.
[18:25] [slight crosstalk] Speaker 3: sorry, go ahead
[18:30] Alicia Gomez: What's the timeline to get the Trust Center items?
[18:35] Jordan Lee: We'll aim to share SOC2 and ISO snapshot by Monday 2025-12-22; Maya will upload the controls mapping and event schema by Sunday 2025-12-21.
[18:50] Tom Reynolds: Can we also schedule a bench run to validate latency for our 1k qps profile?
[18:58] Maya Patel: We'll scope a small benchmark, targeted for the week of Jan 7, 2026 - we'll need sample prompts and expected concurrency.
[19:12] Alicia Gomez: Anything around HIPAA? We didn't get to that but it's critical for PHI in our workflows.
[19:20] Maya Patel: HIPAA-related controls are detailed in a separate compliance pack. We have HIPAA BAAs for enterprise customers; we can share the summary and BAA process.
[19:36] Jordan Lee: Okay, I think we're near time - quick recap and next steps.
[19:45] Jordan Lee: Recap: share SOC2 Type II report, ISO summary, Trust Center link, controls mapping, evidence artifacts, schedule demo and bench run.
[20:00] Alicia Gomez: That works, thanks.
[20:04] Priya Desai: Thanks all.
[20:08] Jordan Lee: We'll follow up via email with attachments.
[20:12] [end of recording]
-- Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-typed acronyms and filler words; timestamps are approximate.
